# What Pragmatism Means
  ¶1 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): SOME YEARS AGO, BEING WITH A CAMPING PARTY IN THE MOUNTAINS, I RETURNED FROM A SOLITARY RAMBLE TO FIND EVERYONE ENGAGED IN a ferocious metaphysical dispute.
  ¶1 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): The corpus of THE DISPUTE was a squirrel--a live squirrel supposed to be clinging to one side of a tree-trunk; while over against the tree's opposite side a human being was imagined to stand.
  ¶1 UNCOVERED: He goes round the tree, sure enough, and the squirrel is on the tree; but does he go round the squirrel?
  ¶1 UNCOVERED: In the unlimited leisure of the wilderness, discussion had been worn threadbare.
  ¶1 UNCOVERED: Everyone had taken sides, and was obstinate; and the numbers on both sides were even.
  ¶1 UNCOVERED: Each side, when I appeared, therefore appealed to me to make it a majority.
  ¶1 PARTIAL (uncovered in CAPS): MINDFUL OF THE SCHOLASTIC ADAGE THAT WHENEVER YOU MEET A CONTRADICTION YOU MUST MAKE A DISTINCTION, I IMMEDIATELY SOUGHT AND FOUND ONE, AS FOLLOWS: "Which party is right," I SAID, "depends on what you PRACTICALLY MEAN by 'going round' the squirrel.
  ¶2 UNCOVERED: Altho one or two of the hotter disputants called my speech a shuffling evasion, saying they wanted no quibbling or scholastic hair-splitting, but meant just plain honest English 'round,' the majority seemed to think that the distinction had assuaged the dispute.
  ¶3 UNCOVERED: I tell this trivial anecdote because it is a peculiarly simple example of what I wish now to speak of as THE PRAGMATIC METHOD.
